ideas.description: Stack the E040 resolution curriculum onto the bs-1536 tip. The tip is E042 (commit 2b85e5e): bs 1536, 6.5 epochs, all at 32 px, SGD-group lr x1.5, Muon lr 0.16 with momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, brightness/contrast jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. Per D012, the E041/E042 commits do not contain the 24 px stage. Check this in the code first; if the tip already has it, skip this idea. Make one change, ported from E040 (commit 18ce8ac). For the first 1.5 epochs (~49 steps at bs 1536), train on whole images bilinearly downsampled to 24 px (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment, after flip, translate and jitter). Then train 5.25 epochs at 32 px, for 6.75 epochs total. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. The whitening-bias freeze stays at the end of epoch 1. The switch falls mid-epoch: use the first half of that epoch's permutation at 24 px and the rest at 32 px, exactly as E040 does. Use F.max_pool2d with a static kernel for each resolution's final pool; do not use amax or flatten().max (E009 bug). In build(), warm up every graph actually used, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035 lesson): 24 px at bs 1536 with and without whitening-bias grad, 32 px at bs 1536 without it, and every partial-batch shape at the 1.5-epoch switch and at the end of the run. Run debug_nan.py on each new graph under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. Compare trial-0 train time with later trials to catch warmup gaps.
ideas.expected: Time 5.20-5.42 s, point ~5.30 s (-2.7% vs 5.449 s). E040 saved 3.0% at bs 1024, and the per-step overhead the curriculum does not touch is a slightly smaller share at bs 1536. Accuracy 0.751-0.759, point ~0.7555 (E040 was +0.08 pp vs its base). If feasible, keep: new best, and I052's 28 px stage then rebases onto it. If it misses 0.753 by <=0.15 pp, keep the code path and pair it with the Muon lr 0.20 idea. A drop >=0.4 pp means low-res epochs interact badly with the fewer, larger steps at bs 1536. In that case, revert and bank the curriculum only at bs 1024.

ideas.description: Win back the bs-1536 accuracy loss through the Muon lr. This is the follow-up pre-registered in I042. At bs 1536 the run takes about 1/3 fewer fixed-magnitude, weight-norm-projected Muon rotations (~212 instead of ~319 steps), so the total rotation path of each filter shrank by about 33%. On the tip (the curriculum-stacked commit if the idea above is kept, else E042), change only the Muon lr for the conv filters, from 0.16 to 0.20. Momentum 0.8, NS3, projection, the schedule shape and floor, the SGD group, lookahead, augmentation and epochs all stay identical. The lr is a 0-d tensor, so nothing recompiles.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp, point +0.12 pp. At bs 1024 the lr axis was flat over 0.16-0.24, with a cliff at 0.36 (E019). Time unchanged within +-1.5%. A gain >=0.2 pp supports the claim that fewer steps want larger rotations. It banks ~0.2 epoch, so the next step is a 0.25-epoch trim of the 32 px phase (~-3.5% time). A drop >=0.25 pp means the cliff moves down at larger batch; then close the Muon-lr axis at 0.16.

ideas.description: Push the batch-size axis one step further, as D012 suggests, after the curriculum stack is settled. On the tip, change only the batch size, from 1536 to 2048, at the same epoch count (~159 steps at 6.5 epochs). Scale every schedule (warmup fraction, decay, Muon lr multiplier, lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp, the whitening-bias freeze at the end of epoch 1 in samples, and the curriculum switch in samples) to the new step count. The Muon lr stays at 0.16 and momentum at 0.8. Scale the SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) per-step lr by x(2048/1536) and keep wd unchanged, the same noise-scale rule E041 used. Lookahead keeps syncing every 5 steps. In build(), warm up the 2048 full batch and the new partial batch (50000 mod 2048 = 848) for every train-graph variant and resolution, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout. Run debug_nan.py on the new shapes and compare trial-0 with later trial times.
ideas.expected: Time -2.5% to -6%, point -4%: ~53 fewer steps of Muon, SGD and lookahead overhead, plus larger GEMMs. Accuracy -0.7 to +0.05 pp, point -0.3 pp: C0113 predicts convex, diminishing returns, and at ~160 steps the run is close to step-limited. A drop <=0.15 pp means keep (feasible at a ~0.2 pp margin). A drop of 0.15-0.35 pp means keep the code and pair it with the next accuracy gain if the exchange rate beats ~0.1 pp per 1%. A drop >=0.35 pp with time down <5% refutes going past 1536 and closes the batch-size axis; then ghost BN at 1536 is the only remaining bs lever.

ideas.description: Test the 'denser averaging' arm of H1.6.1, which is still untested; E028 only lengthened the decay. At bs 1536 a lookahead sync every 5 steps covers 7680 samples, against 5120 at bs 1024, and the run makes only ~42 syncs. On the tip, change only the lookahead sync interval, from every 5 steps to every 3. Change the per-sync base decay from 0.97^5 to 0.97^3 so the per-step decay, and therefore the averaging horizon in steps, is unchanged. The (t/T)^3 ramp, the final-weights handling and everything else stay the same. This holds samples per sync near the bs-1024 value (4608 vs 5120). If the blend is a separate compiled function, nothing new needs warming. If it is inside the train-step graph behind a step-index flag, confirm that both branches are already warmed up.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.2 to +0.35 pp, point +0.07 pp. Time +0.2% to +0.8% (~28 more blends at ~0.7 ms). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.6.1: averaging density matters at large batch (C0152/C0159), and it banks ~0.2 epoch. A result within +-0.15 pp closes the lookahead-schedule axis entirely, since both horizon (E028) and density would then be flat, and H1.6.1 is refuted.

ideas.description: Ghost BatchNorm, which restores the BN batch-statistic noise lost when moving from bs 1024 to 1536 (C0144/C0147). This was the named follow-up in H1.2.3. On the tip, make one change: in training mode, every BatchNorm computes its statistics over 2 ghost groups of half the batch (768 at bs 1536, 424 for the 848-sample final partial batch) instead of the whole batch. Implement it in the BN module's forward: view the input as [G, B/G, C, H, W], compute the per-group mean and biased variance in fp32 over (1,3,4), normalize each group, and apply the affine. Update the running stats with the group-averaged mean and unbiased variance, using the existing momentum. Eval uses running stats exactly as now. Keep it a pure tensor expression with G a Python constant, so Inductor fuses it with no data-dependent branch. Lookahead still blends the buffers. In build(), warm up all train graph variants and shapes with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout. Run debug_nan.py and verify in drafts/ that at G=1 the module matches nn.BatchNorm2d to bf16 tolerance.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.2 to +0.35 pp, point +0.1 pp. Time +0.5% to +3%, point +1.5% (per-group reductions in the Inductor-decomposed BN instead of one full-batch reduction). Supports H1.2.3's ghost-BN mechanism if accuracy rises >=0.2 pp at <=1.5% time; that would also make bs 2048 with 4 ghost groups the follow-up. A gain <0.1 pp, or time >2%, refutes BN noise as the cause of the bs-1536 loss, and the module is dropped.

drop.reason: It was designed as a fallback in case fixed bs 1536 lost more than 0.3 pp. Fixed bs 1536 lost only ~0.18-0.26 pp and is now the tip (E041/E042). A ramp from 1024 to 2048 would be a step back from the current base. The bs-2048 question is now covered by a direct 1536 -> 2048 idea on the tip.

The batch-size direction is settled by E041. 1536 cost ~0.2 pp for -8% time (~0.03-0.05 pp per 1%), much cheaper than cutting epochs. bs 768 would add ~10% time over the tip and could only pay off with a gain of more than ~0.8 pp, which flat-ish per-sample efficiency rules out. Its information value was conditional on I042, which has now been answered.

It was written for the E034 bs-1024 base. The SGD group has since been rescaled x1.5 for bs 1536 (E041), so the 'x64 vs x32' comparison no longer refers to the current per-step rates. H1.7.1's evidence (E039: head lr x0.5 costs 0.41 pp) points toward raising SGD-group rates, not lowering them. I053 (head x2) tests the more promising side first. Re-propose the BN-bias multiplier after I053 if the head axis turns out flat.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E042: bs 1536, 6.5 epochs, all at 32 px, jitter, 5.449 s, 0.7549, margin 0.19 pp. Per D012, E041/E042 do not yet include the E040 24 px curriculum, and E040 by itself saved 3% at no accuracy cost. The top-priority idea (P5) stacks that curriculum onto the bs-1536 tip; expected ~5.30 s at ~0.7555. I052 (the 28 px stage) and I053 (head lr x2) stay queued and apply to whichever commit becomes the tip. I051 (moving the 24 px boundary later, at bs 1024) is still running, and its result tells us how far the low-res phase can be extended.

Two of the new ideas are exploits on the batch-size axis:
- **Muon lr 0.20 at bs 1536 (P3).** This compensates for the run taking a third fewer fixed-magnitude rotations.
- **bs 2048 (P2).** This prices the next step on the batch-size axis, with a pre-registered rule for closing it.

Two are explores on the averaging and BN side, testing whether large batch removed useful noise or averaging density:
- **Lookahead sync every 3 steps with the per-step decay unchanged (P2).** This is H1.6.1's untested density arm.
- **Ghost BN with 2x768 groups (P2).** This is the named follow-up in H1.2.3.

I054 (scheduling how strongly NS orthogonalizes) stays as an explore. Dropped:
- **I047 (bs ramp):** it was a fallback in case fixed bs 1536 lost more than 0.3 pp, and that did not happen.
- **I050 (bs 768):** E041 showed larger batches are the cheaper lever, so going smaller would cost about 10% time for no plausible gain.
- **I048 (BN-bias x32):** it was written for the old bs-1024 SGD rates and points opposite to the E039 evidence; re-propose it after I053.

That leaves 8 queued. The open risk is still the thin margin: H4.1.2/H4.1.3 (extra-seed checks run offline in drafts/) should be done before any epoch trim that leaves less than 0.15 pp of margin.
